description: Oregon-only rules checked against the cited Oregon Revised Statutes. National rules stay in the baseline. No fines.

questions.q: If no designated speed is posted, Oregon's interstate limit in ORS 811.111, other than the named highway segments, is
questions.explanation: ORS 811.111(1)(a) makes it an offense to drive on an interstate, except the portions described in subsection (2), faster than 65 miles per hour, or faster than a different speed posted under ORS 810.180. Paragraph (1)(d)(E) repeats 65 miles per hour on an interstate when no designated speed is posted. Subsection (2) separately sets 70 for most vehicles on a listed stretch of Interstate 84.

questions.q: Oregon's crime of driving under the influence of intoxicants includes a blood alcohol result of
questions.explanation: ORS 813.010(1) says a person commits the offense by driving with 0.08 percent or more by weight of alcohol as shown by a chemical test, by being under the influence of an intoxicant, or by having 0.08 percent or more within two hours after driving without consuming alcohol in the intervening time.

questions.q: Oregon's implied-consent notice says a commercial driver fails the test at
options: 0.04 percent or more in a commercial vehicle
any amount, the same as a driver under 21
questions.explanation: ORS 813.130 tells the person they fail the implied-consent test at 0.08 percent if they were not driving a commercial motor vehicle, at 0.04 percent or more if they were driving a commercial motor vehicle, or at any amount if they were under 21.

questions.q: For a driver under 21, Oregon's implied-consent failure is
options: 0.08 percent, the same as the criminal number
questions.explanation: ORS 813.130 says the person will fail the implied-consent test at any amount if the person was under 21. The criminal DUII section, ORS 813.010, still uses 0.08 percent. The under-21 implied-consent rule is not a 0.02 figure.

questions.q: Oregon revokes a person as a habitual offender for serious crimes when, within five years, the person has
options: six speeding tickets in one year
questions.explanation: ORS 809.600(1) requires revocation as a habitual offender if, within a five-year period, the person has been convicted of three or more of the listed offenses. Those include driving under the influence of intoxicants under ORS 813.010, reckless driving, failure to perform the duties of a driver, and fleeing or attempting to elude.

questions.q: Oregon's other habitual-offender trigger is
questions.explanation: ORS 809.600(2) requires habitual-offender revocation if, within a five-year period, the person has been convicted of 20 or more of the offenses enumerated in subsection (1) or specified in department rules adopted under ORS 809.605.

questions.q: If Oregon's 20th traffic conviction in the five-year count comes two or more years after the previous one,
questions.explanation: ORS 809.600(3) says privileges shall not be revoked under subsection (2) until the 21st conviction within a five-year period when the 20th conviction occurs after a lapse of two years or more from the last preceding conviction. Subsection (5) says a revocation under the section continues for five years from the date of revocation.

questions.q: An Oregon Class C instruction permit may be issued at 15 and is valid for
questions.explanation: ORS 807.280(2)(a) says an applicant must be 15 or older for Class C privileges. Subsection (4) says a Class C instruction driver permit is valid for 24 months from issuance. The holder must have the permit and be accompanied by a person not less than 21 who has a license or endorsement granting the same privileges and who sits beside the holder, unless the permit is for a motorcycle.

questions.q: For the first six months, an Oregon provisional licensee may not carry
options: a passenger under 20 who is not immediate family
more than three passengers of any age
questions.explanation: ORS 807.122(1)(a) says that for the first six months the holder may not operate a vehicle carrying a passenger under 20 who is not a member of the holder's immediate family. For the second six months the holder may not carry more than three passengers under 20 who are not immediate family. Subsection (4) says subsection (1) does not apply to a holder who is 18 or older. A parent, stepparent, or traffic-safety instructor in the vehicle, and a listed farm-employment carpool, are exceptions to the passenger limit.

questions.q: For the first year, an Oregon provisional licensee may not drive
questions.explanation: ORS 807.122(1)(b) bars driving between 12 midnight and 5 a.m. during the first year except when driving between home and work, between home and a school event if no other transportation is available, for employment purposes, or when accompanied by a licensed driver who is at least 25. Subsection (4) says these subsection (1) restrictions do not apply at 18 or older.

questions.q: In Oregon, what is the youngest age at which you can get a learner's permit for a car?
questions.explanation: Oregon issues a learner's permit for a car at 15 years at the earliest.

questions.q: In Oregon, how long must a driver under 18 hold a learner's permit before moving to the next license?
questions.explanation: Oregon requires drivers under 18 to hold the learner's permit for 6 months.

questions.q: How many hours of supervised driving must a teen in Oregon complete before getting a provisional license?
questions.explanation: Oregon requires 100 hours of supervised driving before the provisional license.

provenance.manual: Oregon Driver Manual - Other Important Information

questions.q: In Oregon, what is the youngest age at which a teen can get a license to drive without a supervisor?
questions.explanation: In Oregon, the earliest unsupervised (provisional) license is at 16 years.

provenance.manual: Oregon Driver Manual - Other Important Information

questions.q: During which hours may a newly licensed teen in Oregon not drive without a supervisor?
questions.explanation: Oregon restricts provisional drivers from Midnight to 5 a.m., with exceptions such as work or school.

questions.q: In Oregon, what is the youngest age for a full, unrestricted car license?
questions.explanation: Oregon drivers can hold an unrestricted license at 18 years.

provenance.manual: The Rules for Provisional Driver Licensing

questions.q: How many questions are on the Oregon car knowledge test?
questions.explanation: The Oregon car knowledge test has 35 questions.

questions.q: What score do you need to pass the Oregon car knowledge test?
questions.explanation: You need 80% to pass the Oregon car knowledge test.

questions.q: In Oregon, a driver 21 or older is legally impaired at what blood alcohol concentration?
questions.explanation: In Oregon, drivers 21 and older are over the limit at 0.08% or more.

questions.q: In Oregon, a driver under 21 breaks the law at what blood alcohol concentration?
questions.explanation: Oregon sets the under-21 limit at 0.00%.

questions.q: In Oregon, how long is the license suspension for an adult's first refusal of a breath or blood test?
questions.explanation: A first refusal in Oregon brings a suspension of 1 year.

questions.q: Unless a sign says otherwise, what is the speed limit in a Oregon residential district?
questions.explanation: Oregon sets 25 mph in residential districts unless another limit is posted.

questions.q: What is the highest standard speed limit for cars on rural interstates in Oregon?
questions.explanation: Rural interstates in Oregon can be posted up to 70 mph for cars.

questions.q: Which best describes Oregon's law on drivers using a phone?
options: Phone use is banned only for new or young drivers
Hand-held phone use is banned for all drivers
No statewide ban on phone use or texting
Only texting is banned for all drivers
questions.explanation: Oregon: hand-held phone use is banned for all drivers.

questions.q: When is a left turn on a red light allowed in Oregon?
options: From a one-way or two-way street onto a one-way street
Only from a one-way street onto a one-way street
questions.explanation: In Oregon, a left turn on red (after a full stop, where not prohibited) is allowed: from a one-way or two-way street onto a one-way street.

questions.q: How is Oregon's seat belt law for adults enforced?
options: Primary: police can stop you just for not wearing a seat belt
Secondary: police can cite you only after stopping you for something else
No seat belt law for adults
questions.explanation: Oregon seat belt enforcement is primary.

questions.q: Until what age must a child ride in a car seat or booster seat in Oregon?
questions.explanation: Oregon requires a car seat or booster until 8 years, with height or weight exceptions.

questions.q: What is Oregon's minimum liability insurance (injury per person / injury per crash / property damage)?
questions.explanation: Oregon requires at least $25,000 / $50,000 / $20,000.
